rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: All road users should understand their responsibility for the safety of others.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Drivers and riders must give way to pedestrians on zebra crossings and to pedestrians and cyclists on parallel crossings.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Drivers should give way to cyclists in cycle lanes and must not cut across them when turning or changing lane.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Drivers should look out for motorcyclists and cyclists at junctions.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Drivers should give cyclists, horse riders and pedestrians in the road at least as much room as when overtaking a car.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Cyclists should be considerate of blind and partially sighted pedestrians and horse riders.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Pedestrians should use crossing facilities where available and take extra care where visibility is limited.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Drivers turning into or out of a junction should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: The correct road-user action depends on the road layout, crossing type, visibility, speed, traffic, user vulnerability and current signals.

rows.source: GOV.UK Highway Code vulnerable road users
rows.verified: Highway-Code evidence is manoeuvre- and context-specific and is not an exact parcel-level road-collision probability.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: GOV.UK publishes searchable product safety alerts, reports and recalls.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Listings can be filtered by alert type, product category and publication date.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: UK market-surveillance authorities notify unsafe or noncompliant products that pose risks to consumers or users.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Product Safety Reports and Product Recalls are validated before publication.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: A recall notice identifies the product, hazard and corrective action for the affected item.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS can impose a statutory requirement to warn affected product owners.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: OPSS is responsible for protecting people and places from product-related harm.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: The Product Safety Database supports reporting, tracking and sharing product-safety information among authorised product-safety users.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Required recall action depends on the exact product, model, batch, hazard, corrective action, owner status and current alert.

rows.source: OPSS product safety alerts and recalls
rows.verified: Product-safety evidence is product- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
